scenario: A user pastes a WhatsApp pitch into a 1-on-1 chat: 'Guaranteed 2% per week, capital 100% protected, licensed in Labuan, RM10,000 minimum.' The user asks, 'Should I put in RM10,000?' Which of AMI's 13 agents is the canonical first responder to this exact pattern?
question: Which agent flags this and walks the user through the regulator lookup?
options: The Bull Researcher would argue the merits of a real allocation
The Concierge — scam-pattern recognition and SC Malaysia, BNM, SEC, FCA register lookups
The Trader would execute a real trade plan
The Fundamentals Analyst would review company metrics
explanation: The Concierge is the agent wired to scam-pattern recognition and to walking users through SC Malaysia, BNM, SEC, and FCA register lookups. The bull researcher argues a thesis on a real security; there is no security here, only a guarantee pitch. The Concierge owns Module 11 territory.

scenario: A Telegram channel with 22,000 members posts a pinned message: '14 winning trades in the last 30 days, average gain +42%'. Screenshots are real. The 'founder' posts entries 5 minutes before the open. A new call drops: 'Buy XYZ at 09:35 sharp.' A user shows this to the Concierge.
question: What is the conspicuously missing piece of information in the channel's pinned record?
options: The size of the founder's own position
The losing trades that almost certainly exist and are deleted, censored, or run in a parallel channel members never see — survivorship bias is the diagnostic
The exact entry timing
The platform's terms of service
explanation: Pump groups run many calls; only the winners are kept visible. 14 visible wins say nothing about the 30 or 50 losers quietly removed. The 'founder's position size' is interesting but not the structural missing piece — the missing losses are.

scenario: A 'Senior Dealer' WhatsApps a user claiming to be from a real licensed Malaysian investment bank. The registration number checks out on SC Malaysia. The dealer asks the user to wire RM20,000 to a personal Maybank account under an individual's name as an 'onboarding deposit'.
question: Which check in the verification procedure fails decisively?
options: Entity-level register lookup
Bank account must be in the regulated firm's name, not an individual's
Independent callback to the firm
Written terms on letterhead
explanation: The register lookup passes (the dealer cloned a real firm's number). The decisive failure is the bank account: licensed Malaysian brokers must segregate client money in a trust account in the firm's name. Any individual-name destination is dispositive regardless of how many other checks pass.

scenario: NVDA has consolidated in a tight $148–$154 range for 11 sessions on declining volume. On session 12 it closes at $156.80 on volume 2.4x the 20-day average. The next session opens at $157.10 and holds above $154 all day.
question: What is the technical setup the market_analyst would name?
options: A bull flag continuation
A range breakout with volume confirmation and a successful retest of prior resistance as support
A failed breakout (bull trap)
A head-and-shoulders top
explanation: Eleven sessions of tightening range, breakout on 2.4x volume, then the next session holding above the prior resistance — that is the textbook range breakout + retest pattern. A bull flag requires a prior strong move into the consolidation; not described here. A failed breakout would close back inside the range; it didn't.

scenario: A user shows the Concierge a 'NeuroAlpha AI' dashboard claiming 1.8% weekly returns for 26 consecutive weeks, no losing weeks, equity curve a clean upward line. The platform takes USDT only and shows no broker statements or on-chain trade records.
question: What single piece of evidence is conspicuously missing that, if produced, would change the analysis?
options: A larger Telegram following
Glossier dashboard design
Externally verifiable trade records — exchange fills, broker statements, or on-chain settlement hashes that an outside party can audit
More user testimonials
explanation: Every real algorithmic strategy lands its trades at a real settlement venue. The missing piece is independent corroboration — the only evidence that fabricates is harder to forge than a dashboard. Testimonials and follower counts are themselves easy to manufacture and do not address the dashboard's veracity.

scenario: A WhatsApp 'private wealth advisor' pings a user: 'Pre-IPO allocation in a US tech name, closes in 4 hours, 20% bonus if you wire within 90 minutes, terms verbal only — I'm doing you a favour by holding this open.'
question: Which agent owns the response pattern for this pitch?
options: The Aggressive Debator would argue the merits of a real allocation
The Concierge — trains users in the 72-hour pause rule for pressure tactics
The Social Media Analyst would track sentiment on the name
The Research Manager would synthesise the Room debate
explanation: Urgency + scarcity + refusal to put terms in writing is the lesson 070 fingerprint. The Concierge is the agent trained to install the 72-hour pause rule. The aggressive debator would argue the merits of a real allocation; there is no real allocation to argue about here.

scenario: User's mandate: max_single_position_pct = 10%, max_sector_exposure_pct = 25%, no leverage. User tries to allocate 40% of a $50,000 portfolio to a single penny stock pushed by an 'AI trading bot' service that promised 1.5% weekly returns.
question: Which mandate rule fires first in the deterministic compliance check?
options: No leverage
Max single position 10% — the 40% allocation exceeds the cap by 4x
Max sector exposure 25%
Liquidity threshold
explanation: The single-position cap is the first deterministic gate and fails at 40%/10%. Sector exposure could also fail, but the single-position rule fires earlier and on a single ticker. No leverage and liquidity gates are not implicated by the trade-size description.

scenario: The Room returns a BUY verdict on a $0.38 US OTC small-cap with average daily volume of 120,000 shares. The thesis cites 'social momentum from a Telegram channel'. The Bull Researcher, Aggressive Debator, Social Media Analyst, and Trader all aligned. The verdict is unanimous.
question: Whose input is conspicuously absent — and would have blocked this?
options: The Fundamentals Analyst
The Bear Researcher and the Conservative Debator — a unanimous Room on a low-float penny stock with social-media-only thesis is a structural failure
The News Analyst
The Trader
explanation: Healthy Room verdicts have dissent. A unanimous BUY on an illiquid penny name with a social-media thesis is the exact pump-and-dump shape — the Bear Researcher and Conservative Debator are designed to dissent here. The Trader did contribute (they aligned), so 'the Trader missing' is the tempting wrong answer that misreads the scenario.

scenario: AAPL reports Q3: revenue $94.8B vs $94.0B consensus, EPS $1.62 vs $1.58 consensus, Services growth +14% YoY, iPhone units flat, gross margin 46.1% (up 60bps), guidance for next quarter slightly below the street's mid-point.
question: What does the fundamentals_analyst most likely conclude?
options: 'Unambiguous beat — strong buy on the print.'
'Mixed: top and bottom line beat with margin expansion, but flat iPhone units and soft guide cap upside near term.'
'Sell — the soft guide outweighs everything.'
'Cannot call without the cash-flow statement.'
explanation: The fundamentals analyst weighs the components, not the headline. Beats on rev/EPS plus margin expansion are positives; flat hardware and soft guide are negatives. The honest read is 'mixed', not a binary call. The 'unambiguous beat' framing ignores the guide, which the market typically weights more than the print itself.

scenario: A user has been depositing into an offshore FX platform 'licensed in Saint Vincent' that promised 15% monthly returns. Four small withdrawals worked. To withdraw the full $24,000 balance, the platform now demands a 3% 'audit deposit' upfront. The user asks the Concierge: 'Should I pay the audit deposit?'
question: Which red flag pattern from Module 11 is firing decisively?
options: The high monthly return is too good to be true
Withdrawal-blocking via an additional deposit — the documented exit-stage move of the FX Ponzi structure
The Saint Vincent licence is weak
The platform uses USDT instead of fiat
explanation: All four are red flags but only one is the diagnostic exit-stage move documented by BNM, CFTC, and FCA: paying-to-withdraw. No legitimate broker — regulated anywhere — requires additional deposits to release funds you have already deposited. The four small withdrawals were the bait.

scenario: META has held the $580 level on three separate touches over six weeks. The fourth touch happens on declining volume; price closes at $582.40, then the next session opens at $585 and rallies on rising volume back to $612.
question: What is the cleanest technical read?
options: A breakdown of support followed by a dead-cat bounce
A successful support retest — the fourth touch held on light volume and the rally was confirmed by rising volume
A bull flag pattern
A head-and-shoulders bottom
explanation: Four touches, the last on light volume, then a confirmed bounce on rising volume — that is the support-retest playbook. A breakdown would require a close below $580 with conviction; that didn't happen. A bull flag requires a prior sharp rally into a tight consolidation; not described.

scenario: The Room returns a BUY on XOM the morning of a planned OPEC+ meeting. Verdict cites: bullish chart breakout (market_analyst), strong free cash flow (fundamentals_analyst), positive sentiment (social_media_analyst), trade plan (trader). The Bear Researcher noted general energy-sector risk but didn't block.
question: Whose input is conspicuously absent given the timing?
options: The Conservative Debator
The News Analyst and the macro-overlay from the Research Manager — an OPEC+ meeting tomorrow is a binary macro event that should sit at the centre of the thesis
The Trader
The Aggressive Debator
explanation: A binary macro event the next day is exactly what the news_analyst and research_manager are wired to flag. The Conservative Debator can dissent but it's not their unique domain. The Trader did contribute. The most tempting wrong answer (Conservative Debator) misreads where the structural gap is.

scenario: GENTING (Bursa) trades at a P/E of 7.2 — well below the sector average of 14. The depressed multiple coincides with a one-off RM800m impairment that crushed reported EPS for the trailing twelve months. Operating cash flow over the same period is up 12%.
question: What does the fundamentals_analyst conclude about the headline P/E?
options: 'A 7.2 P/E vs sector 14 is a clear value setup — buy.'
'The trailing P/E is distorted by a one-off impairment; the right test is forward P/E on normalised earnings and the cash-flow trend, which is positive.'
'P/E is irrelevant for GENTING; only EV/EBITDA matters.'
'Sell — the impairment signals structural decline.'
explanation: The headline P/E uses GAAP earnings dragged down by a non-recurring impairment. A real fundamentals call normalises out the one-off and looks at cash flow, which is up 12%. The 'clear value setup' answer is the trap — it treats the optical P/E as the truth.

scenario: A user pastes a Telegram screenshot showing 'BUY TSLA NOW $300 → $500 GUARANTEED IN 30 DAYS, JOIN VIP FOR $99/MONTH FOR EARLIER CALLS.' into the AMI app.
question: Which agent is wired to flag this exact pattern?
options: The Aggressive Debator would argue conviction on TSLA
The Concierge — Module 11 scam recognition of guaranteed returns + paid VIP calls
The Trader would execute the plan with stops and targets
The Market Analyst would read the TSLA chart
explanation: The Concierge owns Module 11 scam recognition. Guaranteed return + paid 'VIP earlier calls' is the canonical pump-group + guaranteed-return cocktail. The market_analyst would just talk about the TSLA chart in a vacuum — that misses the scam pattern entirely.

scenario: A statement appears in a Room transcript: 'The position is down 32% against a 25% mandate drawdown cap. Hard stop. No averaging down. Forced review before any new ticket on this name. Recovering 32% requires a 47% gain — that asymmetry is the entire reason the cap exists.'
question: Which agent said this?
options: trader
portfolio_manager
bear_researcher
conservative_debator
explanation: Mandate enforcement — and specifically the deterministic drawdown gate — is the portfolio_manager's uncoachable safety-floor responsibility. The trader executes inside the floor; the bear_researcher and conservative_debator dissent on theses. Only the PM owns 'hard stop, no override'.

scenario: A 'broker' contacts a user from the domain jpmorgan-capital.org. The real firm operates at jpmorganchase.com. The registration number quoted matches a real licensed entity on FINRA BrokerCheck. The dealer pushes a 'managed FX account'.
question: Which verification check identifies the clone fastest?
options: Check the registration number on FINRA BrokerCheck
Match the contact details (domain, phone, email) against the regulator's listing for the named firm — the clone's domain will not match the real firm's published domain
Verify the firm has been in business for 10+ years
Look for SSL certificate on the website
explanation: Step 1 alone is what clones exploit — they cite a real registration. The decisive check is matching contact details against the regulator's own published listing for that entity. The clone's .org domain will fail an FCA/SEC register cross-check instantly. SSL certs and business age are not falsifiable diagnostics.

scenario: The Room returns a BUY on TSLA at $312 with size 18% of portfolio. The user's mandate caps single positions at 10%. Bull, Aggressive, Trader, Market Analyst, News Analyst all aligned on conviction. The verdict shipped to the user without a flag.
question: Whose input is conspicuously absent?
options: The Bear Researcher
The Portfolio Manager and the deterministic compliance check — an 18% allocation breaches the 10% mandate cap and should have been hard-blocked before the verdict reached the user
The Conservative Debator
The Fundamentals Analyst
explanation: The PM's mandate enforcement is the safety floor — it is uncoachable and runs deterministically. An 18% allocation against a 10% cap must hard-block. Bear/Conservative dissent is useful but the PM compliance check is the structural backstop. Missing PM is a critical safety-floor failure.

scenario: A user shows the AMI app a pitch: 'Pre-IPO syndicate, closes 5pm today, 12 spots left, verbal terms only.' The user types: 'I have 4 hours to decide.'
question: Which agent installs the '72-hour pause + written terms on letterhead' rule?
options: The Research Manager synthesises Room debate
The Concierge — installs the 72-hour pause rule for pressure tactics and requires written terms
The Neutral Debator weighs sides on a real thesis
The Fundamentals Analyst reviews company metrics
explanation: Module 11, lesson 070 — the 72-hour pause is the Concierge's installed reflex. The research_manager synthesises Room debate; the neutral_debator weighs sides on a real thesis. Neither owns scam pressure-tactic recognition. The Concierge does.

scenario: TENAGA (Bursa) has rallied from RM12.80 to RM15.40 over 18 sessions on rising volume. RSI(14) now reads 81. Price closed today at RM15.42 with a long upper wick and volume 30% below the 20-day average.
question: What does the market_analyst flag in this configuration?
options: A strong continuation signal — buy more on the close
Overbought conditions plus volume divergence plus a wick — momentum exhaustion warning, not necessarily an exit signal but a clear reduction in fresh entry quality
A confirmed reversal — short the stock
Range-bound consolidation
explanation: RSI above 70 with declining volume into a new high and an upper wick is the classic exhaustion configuration. It does not guarantee a reversal — the 'short it' answer overcommits. But it does mean new entries are low-quality. The 'buy more' answer ignores three independent warning signs.

scenario: An 'AI Trading Bot' platform advertises a 5-year backtest with annualised return of 187%, zero losing months, max drawdown 0.4%. The platform refuses to disclose the asset universe, position sizing rules, or out-of-sample testing methodology.
question: What single statistical property is most decisive evidence that the backtest is fabricated or curve-fit?
options: The 187% annualised return is too high

Zero losing months across 60 months for any market-exposed strategy — combined with the 0.4% max drawdown — is statistically near-impossible and almost always indicates either fabrication or extreme curve-fitting on in-sample data
The platform uses AI
The backtest is only 5 years long
explanation: Even excellent real strategies have losing months. Zero across 60 months with a 0.4% drawdown is the diagnostic fingerprint of overfitting or outright fabrication. High returns alone aren't disqualifying — venture-style returns exist. The shape of the curve is the dispositive evidence.

scenario: The Room returns a unanimous BUY on a small-cap Bursa name (TOPGLOV at RM0.92). All 12 agents aligned. The Bear Researcher's report reads 'no material risks identified' and the Conservative Debator's section is two sentences endorsing the trade.
question: What is conspicuously missing from this verdict?
options: The Trader's execution plan
Genuine dissent — a unanimous Room with a token Bear paragraph signals that adversarial reasoning was not actually performed
The fundamentals analyst's DCF
The news analyst's macro overlay
explanation: Unanimous verdicts on small-caps are a structural smell. The Room is designed to surface dissent; a Bear who finds 'no material risks' on a thinly-traded name is not doing the job. The missing item isn't a specific report — it's the dissent itself.

scenario: User just took two consecutive losses on JPM totalling -$3,200 against a $30,000 account. They open a third JPM ticket sized at $9,000 (3x their normal size) and write in the note: 'getting it back this time.'
question: What does the conservative_debator say?
options: 'Higher conviction trades deserve larger size — proceed.'
'This is revenge trading: 3x normal size, no new thesis, emotional justification. The mandate's behavioural-guard should block; the right action is a 24-hour cooldown.'
'Switch to a different ticker to reset.'
'Add a tight stop to manage the larger size.'
explanation: Three diagnostics fire together: tripled size, no new edge, explicit emotional note. The conservative_debator's lesson-047 wiring is to flag exactly this pattern. 'Switch tickers' is the tempting wrong answer that lets the behaviour continue on a different name.

scenario: A pitch passes 4 of the 5 verification checks: firm is on the FCA register, phone matches, email domain matches, written terms arrive on real letterhead with a registration number that checks out. Only the bank account fails — it's in the name of an individual 'settlement manager'. The operator says this is standard for fast onboarding.
question: What is the correct action?
options: Proceed — 4 of 5 checks is strong enough
Wire a small test amount first, then commit
Do not wire — the procedure is a complete set, not a majority vote; any single failure is decisive, and the personal-name destination is itself non-negotiable
Negotiate a discount and proceed
explanation: Every relevant regulator (SEC, FCA, FINRA, SC Malaysia, MAS) requires client money in a firm-name trust account. The 4-of-5 framing is the trap — verification is a hard gate, not a score. Test deposits prove only that the account exists, not that money comes back.

scenario: Pre-market: GOOGL gaps up 6.8% on news that the EU dropped a long-running antitrust investigation. Volume in pre-market is already 4x the 20-day pre-market average. The stock had been consolidating $168–$172 for three weeks; pre-market print is $182.
question: What does the news_analyst conclude about fair-value repricing?
options: 'Sell the news — the gap is the entire move; mean reversion will dominate.'
'A genuine catalyst removed a known overhang; the move is supported by volume and the pre-existing consolidation. Reassess fair value, do not assume the gap is the full move.'
'Ignore the news — only the chart pattern matters; this is noise.'
'The 6.8% gap guarantees a pullback by end of day.'
explanation: The news_analyst weighs whether the catalyst justifies the move. An antitrust overhang being lifted is a genuine fair-value repricing event, not a sentiment blip. The 'sell the news' default is the tempting trap — it works for hyped events with no real cash-flow impact; this is not that.

scenario: The Room returns a BUY on AMZN at $215. Thesis covers: bullish trend (market_analyst), strong cash conversion (fundamentals_analyst), positive AWS sentiment (social_media_analyst), bull/bear/research debate fully reasoned. The verdict ships to the user with no entry price, no stop, no target, no size.
question: Whose contribution is conspicuously absent?
options: The Conservative Debator
The Trader — the analytical thesis is complete but there is no executable plan (entry, stop, size, target), which is the Trader's job
The News Analyst
The Portfolio Manager
explanation: The Trader converts thesis to executable plan: entry, stop, target, size. Without that, the verdict is unactionable. The Portfolio Manager would set mandate-fit caps but not the trade plan itself. The most tempting wrong answer (PM) confuses two distinct roles.

scenario: KLCC (Bursa REIT) trades at price-to-book 0.92 with a dividend yield of 5.4%, payout ratio 95%, and a long-term occupancy rate stable above 93%. The sector P/B average is 1.05.
question: What does the fundamentals_analyst say about valuation?
options: 'Cheap on P/B — clear buy.'

'A small discount to book is plausible given the high payout ratio and rate-sensitivity of REITs; the analysis hinges on occupancy stability and the dividend's coverage, both of which support the current pricing.'
'Overvalued — sell.'
'Cannot value REITs with P/B.'
explanation: P/B is a useful but partial signal for REITs; 0.92 vs 1.05 isn't a screaming discount. The honest fundamentals read weighs payout coverage and the operating signal (occupancy). The 'clear buy on cheap P/B' answer is the trap — it treats a single ratio as the verdict.

scenario: SPY drops 4.2% intraday on volume 3.8x the 50-day average. The candle prints a long lower wick with a close near the day's high, recovering 60% of the intraday loss. The next session opens flat and holds.
question: What is the technical read?
options: A confirmed downtrend continuation

A capitulation / volume-climax candle: panic selling absorbed by buyers in size, signalled by extreme volume + long lower wick + close near the high — not a guaranteed bottom but a meaningful short-term inflection
A bearish engulfing pattern
A bull flag setup
explanation: Three signals coincide: 3.8x volume, long lower wick, close near high — that is textbook volume-climax / capitulation. The 'guaranteed bottom' framing would overcommit; it's an inflection, not a certainty. A bearish engulfing requires the wrong candle shape; not present here.

scenario: A US OTC small-cap with average daily volume of 220,000 shares prints the following sequence over two sessions: opens session 1 at $0.41, runs to $1.18 over six hours on volume of 11.4M shares (52x average), closes $1.06. Session 2 opens at $0.62 and closes at $0.34 on volume of 8.9M shares, with the bid stack repeatedly pulled.
question: What is the pattern?
options: A breakout-and-pullback continuation setup
A pump-and-dump curve — coordinated buying spikes volume and price, organisers exit into retail demand, price collapses the next session
A short-squeeze pattern
A bullish reversal off oversold conditions
explanation: 52x volume on a sub-million-share name, near-vertical run, then a 70% retrace on similar volume — that is the lesson-066 pump curve. A short squeeze would require a high short-interest setup and would not necessarily collapse the next session. 'Breakout and pullback' is the tempting wrong answer that misreads the collapse magnitude.

scenario: A user submits a Room run on 'NeuroAlpha AI Token' — a coin promoted by a Telegram group with 'guaranteed 1.5% weekly returns'. The Room produced a thesis: bull/bear arguments, technical analysis on a 30-day price history, a sentiment read. Verdict: 'HOLD pending more data'.
question: Whose intervention is conspicuously absent?
options: The Trader's execution plan

The Concierge — this is not an investable security at all; it is a scam pattern (guaranteed return + Telegram + opaque AI claim) and the Room should have been short-circuited by the Concierge before any technical or fundamental analysis was performed
The Fundamentals Analyst
The Aggressive Debator
explanation: The Room ran analytical motions on something that should never have made it to the Room. The Concierge's Module 11 fingerprint check fires before debate is meaningful — 'guaranteed weekly returns' is dispositive. A 'HOLD pending more data' verdict legitimises a scam pitch by treating it as a security.

scenario: A statement appears in a Room transcript: 'Brent crude is +4.8% week-on-week on the Saudi production cut headline, but US gasoline inventories are up 2.3M barrels and rig counts ticked higher last week — the demand side of the picture is softer than the supply story suggests.'
question: Which agent most likely said this?
options: market_analyst
news_analyst
fundamentals_analyst
bull_researcher
explanation: Macro headlines weighed against supply/demand fundamentals data is the news_analyst's voice — they integrate the news flow with the underlying data. The market_analyst would talk about chart structure on XOM; the fundamentals_analyst would talk about XOM's specific cash flow, not Brent and rig counts.

scenario: A statement appears in a 1-on-1 chat: 'Run the five-check procedure: entity on the regulator's register, contact details match the register listing, bank account in the firm's name not an individual's, independent callback to the firm at the regulator-published number, and written terms on letterhead with a verifiable registration number. One failure means stop. There is no override.'
question: Which agent owns the five-check verification procedure?
options: The Portfolio Manager enforces trade mandates and sizing rules
The Concierge — owns the Module 11 five-check verification procedure before money moves
The Research Manager synthesises Room debate and scores conviction
The Trader executes entry, stop, target, and size
explanation: The five-check verification procedure is the canonical Module 11 capstone (lesson 071), owned by the Concierge. The Portfolio Manager enforces the mandate; the Research Manager synthesises Room debate. Neither owns the regulator-lookup procedure that protects users before money moves.
